1) If a request payload includes the key "title" the request must be rejected with HTTP 422; presence of "title" must cause rejection even when "name" is present.
2) Create (POST) operations: "name" is required.
3) Update (PATCH/PUT) operations: "name" may be omitted.
4) Responses must continue to include both "title" and "name" fields (response payloads still provide both keys).
5) Preserve all existing "name" constraints (type, length and nullability) unchanged.
6) Do not silently ignore the old key: do not silently strip or drop client-supplied "title" before signalling the error.

Frontend implementation instructions:

   - Add a client-side validation rule that detects the presence of the key "title" in the form/model/payload that will be sent to any create (POST) or update (PUT/PATCH) requests for the resource(s) in scope.
   - If "title" is present, block the submit and show a validation error to the user matching a 422-level problem (e.g., visible field-level error tied to the UI component that produced the title input or a global validation banner). The message must clearly state that the "title" key is no longer accepted and the request would be rejected with 422.
   - Do NOT silently remove or strip "title" from the outgoing payload. The client must surface the fact that "title" was supplied and must be corrected by the user.
   - Ensure the UI prevents sending any request containing the "title" key (the network client should not trim the key automatically before sending). If existing client code auto-injects or maps a local "title" property into API payloads, change that mapping to cause a client-side validation failure instead of silent removal.

2) Create vs Update behavior in the UI and client serializers:
   - Create forms: enforce "name" as required using the existing frontend validation for "name" (type/length/nullability must match existing rules). Do not alter the existing constraints; reuse current validators.
   - Update forms: allow "name" to be omitted. Do not mark "name" as required on edit; allow the user to submit without touching the name field. When the UI allows partial updates, ensure that omission translates to omission in the request payload (but only when omission is deliberate and not because of silent stripping of fields the user provided).

3) Response handling and display:
   - Continue to read and render both "title" and "name" from server responses where they are present. Do not drop rendering of "title" from read/display code; the change is only about rejecting "title" in requests.
   - If the backend returns 422 for a request containing "title", surface the server error to the user using the existing client-side error rendering pattern.

   - Add unit/integration tests for each affected create/update UI and API client that assert: (a) supplying a payload containing "title" triggers client-side validation and blocks submission, (b) client does not silently strip "title", and (c) attempting to send still results in a surfaced 422 behaviour if server returns 422.
   - Add tests verifying create flow requires "name" (using existing name constraints) and update flow allows omitting "name".
   - Add end-to-end tests that verify responses still include and display both "title" and "name".

5) Developer documentation and logs:
   - Update client-side developer docs and API usage guides to state that sending "title" in requests is rejected (422) and that create requires "name" while update may omit it.
   - Add instrumentation/logging when a user attempts to submit with "title" so that product/engineering can monitor how often legacy clients supply "title".

6) Rollout notes:
